posts.text: 📝 Betting on the North 📝 Russia revises its Arctic development strategy Just a few decades ago, most countries' interest in the Arctic was limited to scientific research and prospects for raw material extraction. Today, even states without access to the Arctic Ocean are competing for the opportunity to establish a foothold in the region. Amid growing competition, Vladimir Putin approved a new strategy for developing the Arctic zone through 2035 with prospects extending to 2050. 🔻 Key objectives : ▪️ Increase the Arctic's share in the combined GRP of Russian regions to 8.4%, and in total Russian capital investment to 12.6%. ▪️ Bring annual cargo flow along the Northern Sea Route to 110–150 million tons. ▪️ Within six months, develop a comprehensive project for Arctic zone development and the Trans-Arctic transport corridor. ▪️ Strengthen Russia's military potential in the region. These plans will need to be implemented under challenging conditions. Western sanctions failed to halt existing Russian projects, but significantly slowed their expansion. In November, cargo flow along the Northern Sea Route exceeded 40 million tons for the first time, although initial plans called for reaching 110 million tons by 2025. 📌 Moreover, economic pressure accompanies NATO's strengthened military presence . All Arctic states, except Russia, now belong to the alliance, and since February, the bloc's command coordinates allied activities under the Arctic Sentry initiative. Competition is growing in other areas as well. The USA, Canada, and Finland jointly develop icebreaker shipbuilding, while Chinese authorities seek to establish a foothold in the region through participation in energy and transport projects. ❗️ The Arctic holds strategic importance for Russia from both economic and military perspectives. Therefore, it is especially important to strengthen Russia's own positions in the region now, when all other Arctic states are united in the idea of reducing Russian influence in the region. #Russia #USA #China ✉️ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

"If you ask the Grok AI and several others which country in the world has the largest amount of available electric power for data centers and at the lowest price, Russia is the number one country globally. This is linked to our gas reserves and the already installed capacities of the Russian power grid," he said. The developed nuclear power industry is also a contributing factor, Dmitriev noted.
